content.text: Do you have some verbiage about test-driven development you'd like to contribute to the end you propose?
My apologies, I have already updated the documentation with the following:
We like tests. We use JUnit and Mockito (and, sometimes, reluctantly, PowerMockito.) HTTP Integration tests use grizzly.

Ensuring that the quality of the code base is maintained (as it is extended, refactored, or otherwise modified) can be addressed through the extensive coverage of functionality by unit or integration testing.  One approach often undertaken within the domain of software development is that of test driven development, in which the appropriate testing suites outlining the behavior of some method are structured concurrently or before the method itself is actually implemented.  Adhering to this methodology is by no means mandatory, but it does often assist in ensuring that the code base is quality assured to a higher degree.
Please let me know if this is not the preferred approach, and I shall revert the Page to the previous version (removing my modifications) immediately.
That's fine with me-- the important point is to be explicit that TDD is not in any way a requirement for working on Fedora. If you know of a good tutorial for TDD, you might want to link it there.
the important point is to be explicit that TDD is not in any way a requirement for working on Fedora
I completely understand, I can work to greater ensure that this is the case.
If you know of a good tutorial for TDD, you might want to link it there.
Certainly, I shall look to find such a resource (preferably, one specific to working with Mockito).
No, I think your language is fine. It comes across as a helpful suggestion, which is what we want. Please do link something there if you find something you like.

On the main topic of test examples, is there a Confluence macro to pull code from Github? I'm a little troubled by the burden of keeping any more than one source code resource up to date. It's not something we never do, but it would be better to "import" or "quote" code from the actual codebase. It would keep us honest, too.
Here is a premium git/confluence plugin:
https://marketplace.atlassian.com/plugins/nl.avisi.confluence.plugins.git-plugin
, could we try that out to see if it's any good? Is that something you can do, or is it someone else at DuraSpace?
I have contacted Atlassian regarding licensing.
Work to date by
https://wiki.duraspace.org/pages/diffpagesbyversion.action?pageId=34655501&selectedPageVersions=10&selectedPageVersions=7
, Do you see a button on this ticket labelled "Start Work". If so, please push it. If not, please let me know.
, I added the "Git For Confluence" plugin. See the following update (duplicate file currently displayed), and see what you think:
https://wiki.duraspace.org/pages/diffpagesbyversion.action?pageId=34655501&selectedPageVersions=10&selectedPageVersions=11
The obvious downside is that there does not appear to be a way to select a portion of a file.
thank you very much for this.  I believe that this is indeed quite an improvement, and appears to address the concerns voiced by

I'm a little troubled by the burden of keeping any more than one source code resource up to date. It's not something we never do, but it would be better to "import" or "quote" code from the actual codebase. It would keep us honest, too.
Unfortunately, attempting to set the "firstline" property of the macro setting does, as you indicated, fail to select a portion of the file being integrated into the Page.

However, given that the examples are structured within "expand" macro blocks, I believe that these shortcoming does not offset the advantages present in ensuring that the documentation does not fall out of parity with the code base itself.
, thanks. Please finish updating the wiki page(s) with this macro, then click the button "Start Review" on this ticket when you are done. If you do not see such a button, please let me know.

thank you for your patience, the Page has been updated.  Unfortunately, I do not believe that the "Start Review" button is accessible for me (I attempted this while the Issue was in progress, after I've stopped the progress for the issue, and after I've refreshed the page in browser clients).
Resolved with:
https://wiki.duraspace.org/pages/diffpagesbyversion.action?pageId=34655501&selectedPageVersions=12&selectedPageVersions=7
Within the page
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FF/Guide+for+New+Developers
it would perhaps be desirable to integrate examples from the code base when referencing the design patterns and frameworks utilized for testing.

Further, it could also be of some value to reference methodological aims regarding the practice of test-driven development (in a manner such that potential contributors are encouraged to maintain or increase the quality of the code base).
